LFM2_FAMILY_TRANSFER.question: LFM2-24B-A2B (discovered earlier this session) is conv + sparse-attention + MoE. Do the SMALL LFM2.5 bodies keep the conv/attention hybrid, and do they keep the MoE?
LFM2_FAMILY_TRANSFER.answer: the conv/attention hybrid TRANSFERS and the MoE does NOT. LFM2.5-1.2B is 10 conv / 6 attention and LFM2.5-2.6B is 22 conv / 8 attention -- both dense, no expert tensors at all, where the 24B carried MoE FFN on 38 of 40 layers. So 'LFM2 = triple hybrid' is wrong as a family rule: the conv+attention token-mixing split is the family trait, and MoE is a scale-tier choice layered on top of it only at the large end.
LFM2_FAMILY_TRANSFER.why_it_matters_for_gravity: a rule keyed on 'LFM2 -> attack the expert organ' would find no expert organ here and silently do nothing. Architecture-family rules must be keyed on measured structure, not on the family NAME.

RESIDENT_PULSAR_ANATOMY_per_S003.context_observation: both LFM2.5 bodies advertise 128000-token context at 1.2B/2.6B -- far beyond anything else in this size class here (Falcon3-1B 8192, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B 32768) and beyond the CURRENT RESIDENT's own 8192 max_seq_len. Context servability is an explicit S003 judging axis, and experiment 1's campaign hit the 8192 ceiling hard enough to need an admission guard -- so this is the one axis where a small body plausibly beats the 27B outright. RESIDENT_PULSAR_ANATOMY_per_S003.embedding_overhead_warning: Falcon3-1B spends a large share of a small budget on a 131072-entry vocabulary, and Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B likewise on 151669 -- at this scale the embedding table is a first-order term, not a rounding error, which inverts the usual assumption that the transformer stack dominates.
disqualified_for_resident: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B -- an EMBEDDING model: it scores text, it does not generate or call tools, so it cannot run a WorkUnit at all. Retained as a possible CEPHEID (independent calibrator) only.
